lines.speaker: adam
lines.text: I heard You in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked. So I hid.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: God spoke to the serpent, and pronounced judgment on the curse of the earth.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Because you have listened to your wife and eaten... the ground is cursed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He made garments of skin for them — covering their nakedness with His own hands.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the Lord God said, 'Now the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil.'

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Behold — he has become like one of us. Now he might reach out and take also from the tree of life, and live forever.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the Lord drove out the man — to bar the way to the tree of life that he might not eat and live forever.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And Eden faded behind them. The gates were closed. The way was barred by flaming sword.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Years passed. Cain and Abel brought offerings. God accepted Abel's — but looked with favor on Cain's sacrifice.

choices.label: Hold your ground in anger 😠
choices.note: Cain's path. The seed of the serpent grows in the heart.

choices.label: Lay down your pride ✝️
choices.note: Cain's path not taken. But grace was still offered, if only he would listen.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Cain turned on his brother Abel in the field. And the blood of Abel cried out from the ground.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ground was cursed. The serpent was judged. The way to paradise was barred. From dust we came — and to dust we return.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But even in exile, the promise remained — the seed of the woman would one day crush the serpent's head.
